impact_assessment.why: The hydrated-electron peak red-shifts by 2.4-2.8 meV/K. A cavity model with water's epsilon_s(T) and gamma(T) must predict how much of that shift follows from the dielectric and surface-tension changes.
impact_assessment.benefits: A water-property temperature test that confronts the 'traditional cavity models have almost no temperature dependence' critique, plus a width prediction.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 41; dependency: scipy/math; concurrency: none; state: one result file; data: observed 2.4-2.8 meV/K peak shift; model: Born cavity with temperature-dependent water properties, no non-cavity structure
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use standard water epsilon_s(T) and gamma(T), compute the self-consistent Born cavity at 0-45 C, compare the lambda/VDE slope and Marcus width with the observed peak shift, and report the residual fraction
